Eva, Marissa — pulled an initial sketch together based on the CSV and the Qs above. Sending a very conservative first-pass estimate; we can refine once we have token histograms and per-endpoint splits. Attachment: quick-sizing-estimate.xlsx

Key assumptions I used (please confirm):
- Baseline mix: 60% chat (stateful), 30% completion/search, 10% batch embeddings/rerank.
- Chat: median prompt 110 tokens, median response 420 tokens. Completion/search: median prompt 60 / response 180. Embeddings: average 1.2k tokens batch jobs.
- Average tokens per second per request (chat): ~20 tps during generation.
- Average concurrency during 95th percentile minute: 420 simultaneous chat streams across the fleet (estimate from CSV extrapolation).
- KV-cache hit rate assumed 88% (6% cold as reported).

Sizing guidance (high level):
- For chat-heavy workloads with 99P latency target <=300ms, we recommend reserving a mix of H100 and A100-80GB nodes. H100 for the largest variants and low-latency tails; A100 for quantized 8-bit variants to reduce cost.
- Map: 1 H100 node (4-GPU pod) can sustain ~1,600 concurrent lightweight chat streams (with aggressive batching and 8-bit quantization). For conservative planning, use 1,000 concurrency per 4x-GPU H100 pod.
- Buffer: include a 30% reserved headroom for promotional bursts and model migration overhead.

Operational notes:
- Continuous batching improves utilization but increases 99P tail. For your 300ms 99P SLO we'd recommend hybrid: aggressive batching up to 50ms and then a priority lane for latency-sensitive token slices.
- Cold-cache events are expensive; if Nebula can seed session KV for top 10% of active users prior to promotions, we can reduce effective GPU count by ~8–10%.

I'll turn this into a formal proposal with a per-month committed GPU count and cost delta once we get the token histograms.
